text:
The night pressed against David Vance’s office window, a heavy, velvet cloak. Beneath the old floorboards, a low hum vibrated, a frequency just shy of audible, a ghost note. It wasn't the town's usual groan; this was deeper, a resonant ache in the earth itself that made his coffee cup shiver imperceptibly on the desk. He traced a finger along the rim, the ceramic cool against his skin, trying to anchor himself in the concrete. The papers scattered before him offered little comfort, only more questions.

He clicked on the ancient reel-to-reel, the tape spooling with a familiar hiss. But instead of the clear interview he’d recorded, a wash of static bled through, carrying with it fragmented whispers—voices tangled and distorted, like garbled commands lost in a storm. The single bare bulb above his head flickered in sympathy, a sudden, erratic stutter against the deep shadow. It wasn't just old wiring; the whole building seemed to hold its breath, then exhale with a sigh of failing circuitry, a momentary glitch in the fabric of the damp air.

David leaned closer, straining to discern meaning in the noise, but it was just sound without sense, a chorus of wrongness. Blackwood Bay had always hummed with a hidden current, but lately, the static was growing louder, the tremors more insistent. He looked at the photographs spread across his desk—missing persons, strange carvings, the ever-present, unblinking eye of the lighthouse cutting through the coastal fog. This wasn't just a string of unfortunate events; something was pulling at the threads, unraveling the edges of the town, and tonight, it felt like the very air was starting to fray.
